Validating rFIA against EVALIDator

Jeffrey W. Doser

September 25, 2026

Source: vignettes/evalidatorValidation.Rmd
evalidatorValidation.Rmd

Overview

EVALIDator is the USDA Forest Service’s online tool for producing population estimates from the FIA Database (FIADB). Its estimates are the reference that FIA analysts and users compare against, so rFIA must reproduce them. The rFIA unit tests check estimates from the package’s main estimation functions against values from EVALIDator for a range of common estimation settings. This document summarizes the results of those tests and keeps a record of how the tests have performed over time.

How the comparisons work

Each comparison test has the same structure:

  1. Data. We read FIADB data for four states, one from each FIA region: Rhode Island (Northern), North Carolina (Southern), Colorado (Interior West), and Oregon (Pacific Northwest). We then subset each state to its most recent evaluation with clipFIA(mostRecent = TRUE).
  2. Reference values. At test time, reference values come from the FIADB-API fullreport endpoint, the programmatic interface behind EVALIDator. We request the same evaluation group (EVAL_GRP), attribute (e.g., aboveground biomass of live trees on forest land), and domain filter (e.g., a physiographic class filter for areaDomain, or a species filter for treeDomain) that the rFIA call uses.
  3. Comparison. rFIA is run with the temporally indifferent estimator (the default method = 'TI'), which is the method EVALIDator uses. Point estimates and percent sampling errors must match EVALIDator to within a relative tolerance of 10-6. Where EVALIDator reports them, the number of non-zero plots used in the numerator and denominator of ratio estimates must match exactly.

The settings tested include the default case for each function, landType and treeType variants, biomass and carbon components, treeDomain and areaDomain filters, and per-species estimates (bySpecies = TRUE). One test is an approximate comparison rather than an exact one: growMort() for Oregon timberland. It checks that a known, documented discrepancy stays below 1% (see Known EVALIDator discrepancies). The full test code is in tests/testthat/ of the rFIA GitHub repository. The analysis behind each function’s tests is described in core_references/validation/.

A test is recorded as skipped, not failed, when the FIADB-API cannot be reached. A skip means the comparison did not run, not that rFIA disagreed with EVALIDator.

How this document is updated

The full rFIA test suite runs on a regular schedule (every 2 weeks) in addition to automated testing via GitHub. This document is updated each time a new log file is generated.

This version was generated from 1 test log(s) found in ~/rfia-test-logs, covering runs from 2026-09-24 19:17 to 2026-09-24 19:17.

Known EVALIDator discrepancies

In one case, rFIA deliberately does not reproduce EVALIDator. We describe it below, along with why we chose not to match EVALIDator.

Timberland growth and mortality in states that use macroplots

Affected functions: growMort() and vitalRates() with landType = 'timber'.

Affected states: states whose condition proportions are measured on the macroplot, mainly in the Pacific Northwest (e.g., Oregon, Washington, and California). Estimates for forest land (landType = 'forest', the default) match EVALIDator exactly in every state. Timberland estimates match EVALIDator exactly in Rhode Island, North Carolina, and Colorado, which have no macroplot-based conditions.

Size of the discrepancy: at the time of the investigation (August 2026, Oregon evaluation group 412203), rFIA counted 7,788 plots in the Oregon timberland area denominator, compared with 7,749 in EVALIDator. This is a difference of 39 plots (about 0.5%). The resulting per-acre estimates differ by about 0.09%. For example, annual mortality was 1.672704 trees per acre in rFIA and 1.671130 in EVALIDator, and aboveground biomass growth was 1.367651 in rFIA and 1.366364 in EVALIDator. Plot counts differed by a similar margin in California (2,580 vs. 2,562) and Washington (4,899 vs. 4,870).

What causes the difference

Growth, removal, and mortality estimates are ratios. The denominator is the area of land that was in the same land class (forest land or timberland) at both the previous and current measurements of a plot. FIA estimates this area from the SUBP_COND_CHNG_MTRX table, which records the proportion of each subplot or macroplot that moved between condition classes between the two measurements. Each condition’s area proportion is measured on either the subplot (COND.PROP_BASIS = 'SUBP') or the larger macroplot (PROP_BASIS = 'MACR'). The FIA Population Estimation User Guide (Chapter 7.8) says to take the change proportions from the matching plot component: SUBPTYP = 1 rows for subplot-based conditions and SUBPTYP = 3 rows for macroplot-based conditions.

rFIA applies this rule to both forest land and timberland. We obtained the SQL that EVALIDator runs for these estimates (the FIADB-API returns it with each estimate) and found that EVALIDator is not consistent between the two land classes:

  • For the forest land denominator, EVALIDator applies the same subplot/macroplot rule as rFIA, and the two agree exactly.
  • For the timberland denominator, EVALIDator only reads the subplot rows (SUBPTYP = 1), so change on macroplot-based conditions is never read. It then multiplies these subplot proportions by the macroplot adjustment factor (ADJ_FACTOR_MACR) for macroplot-based conditions. A subplot proportion scaled by a macroplot adjustment factor does not correspond to a meaningful area.

Why rFIA does not reproduce EVALIDator here

We decided to keep the rFIA behavior for the following reasons:

  1. It follows the documented method. rFIA implements the rule from the FIA Population Estimation User Guide. We found no documentation that gives a reason for leaving macroplot-based timberland out of the growth-accounting area, and our own assessment of the database logic is in line with the rFIA implementation.
  2. It is consistent across land classes. EVALIDator uses the subplot/macroplot rule for forest land but not for timberland. Reproducing it would make rFIA treat the two land classes differently for no reason beyond simply matching EVALIDator.
  3. The effect is small and limited. The difference is under 1% and only occurs for timberland in states that use macroplot-based conditions.

How the tests handle it

The growMort() tests compare Oregon timberland mortality to EVALIDator approximately: they check that the relative difference stays below 1%, so the test will catch any growth in the discrepancy. The vitalRates() timberland comparisons run only for Rhode Island, North Carolina, and Colorado, where the two agree exactly.
